name: The Hundred Cities
what_happened: every valley held a city-state with its own patron, temple and king
what_it_means_now: the patrons were NAMED PARTIES WITH TERMS, not metaphors
how_the_game_uses_it: flashback chapters F1-F3: different roster, chariots, no requisition, no permadeath

name: The Binding of Sargath
shape: Sargath of Ur-Nashet binds the rest
what_happened: the First Register is written: which patron owes what to whom
what_it_means_now: every pact in the present is a clause in a treaty nobody alive negotiated
how_the_game_uses_it: the founding crime; the demons the nobles borrow from are deposed city-patrons

name: The Long Reign
what_happened: the church that held it together was not telling the truth
what_it_means_now: learning moved east and came back translated; the capital lived on inheritance
how_the_game_uses_it: the age the Diadem still thinks it is living in

name: The Venerated
shape: a person, and then an absence
what_happened: what they did is disputed; whether they died is disputed; the tomb is disputed
what_it_means_now: the sects are five answers to one question the game never settles
how_the_game_uses_it: no depiction survives that all parties accept as authentic

name: The War of the Two Claims
what_happened: crowned succession against elective succession; both call themselves the inheritance
what_it_means_now: ended in exhaustion, not victory; the claim did not end
how_the_game_uses_it: Act 1 opens in the year after

name: Sargath, the binder
shape: a city-king who made the first empire and the first register in the same act
what_happened: he did not kill the patrons; he WROTE THEM DOWN, which turned gods into signatories
what_it_means_now: the register is his instrument and it outlived his empire by seven centuries
how_the_game_uses_it: named for a real child; the sound is right and the etymology is nobody's
